metadata.description: Comprehensive information about horse behavior, movements, and communication

herd_dynamics.description: Social structure and organization in natural horse herds

structure.description: Dominant female who leads the herd to resources
Dominant male who protects the herd
characteristics: Defends against predators and other stallions
Young males often form bachelor groups

herd_dynamics.hierarchy: Established and maintained through body language and occasional physical confrontations

feeding_patterns.grazing_time: 10-17 hours per day in natural settings
feeding_patterns.grazing_style: Continuous small meals, moving slowly while eating
feeding_patterns.selection: Prefer certain grasses and plants, avoid eating near manure
feeding_patterns.water_needs: 8-12 gallons per day, prefer clean, fresh water

rest_patterns.sleep_requirements: 2-3 hours of total sleep in 24-hour period

sleep_types.description: Light sleep while standing using the stay apparatus
Lying down on the sternum with legs tucked under
Lying flat on the side, deep sleep
sleep_types.duration: 10-30 minutes at a time, rarely exceeding 30 minutes

rest_patterns.security_needs: Require feeling safe to enter deep sleep phases

mare_estrus.duration: 5-7 days every 21 days during breeding season

foaling.description: Behavior before, during, and after birth
foaling.foaling_process: Usually occurs at night, takes 15-30 minutes once active labor begins

flight.description: Primary defense strategy, running from perceived threats
flight.distance: Flight distance varies by individual and experience
flight.speed: Can reach 40 mph (64 km/h) in short bursts

fight.description: Secondary defense when flight not possible

freeze.function: Allows for threat evaluation before deciding to flee

vocalizations.name: Nicker
vocalizations.context: Greeting, anticipation of food, mare to foal communication

vocalizations.name: Whinny/Neigh
vocalizations.context: Calling to distant horses, anxiety when separated from herd

vocalizations.name: Squeal
vocalizations.context: Warning, aggressive encounters, mare rejecting stallion

vocalizations.name: Snort
vocalizations.description: Forced expulsion of air through nostrils
vocalizations.context: Alertness, excitement, or clearing nasal passages

vocalizations.name: Blow
vocalizations.description: Softer expulsion of air than snort

vocalizations.name: Groan
vocalizations.context: Pain, extreme exertion, sometimes pleasure during grooming

tail.meaning: Excitement, alertness, may indicate high energy
Irritation, fly control, can escalate to aggression

overall_posture.description: Muscles tight, body stiff, ready for flight
Soft eyes, relaxed muscles, may have a leg rested
Head and neck extended, ears pinned, may swing hindquarters toward target

mutual_grooming.description: Horses using teeth to scratch each other's withers, back, and neck
mutual_grooming.social_function: Bonding, stress reduction, practical help with itching

natural_gaits.name: Walk
natural_gaits.description: Four-beat gait with each foot hitting ground separately
natural_gaits.footfall_pattern: Right hind, right front, left hind, left front
characteristics: Most efficient gait for energy conservation
Always has at least two feet on ground

natural_gaits.name: Trot
natural_gaits.footfall_pattern: Left front and right hind together, right front and left hind together

natural_gaits.name: Canter
natural_gaits.description: Three-beat gait with a moment of suspension
natural_gaits.footfall_pattern: First beat: outside hind leg. Second beat: inside hind and outside fore together. Third beat: inside fore, followed by suspension
characteristics: Can be right or left lead

natural_gaits.name: Gallop
natural_gaits.description: Fastest gait, four-beat with a moment of suspension
natural_gaits.speed: 25-30 mph (40-48 km/h), top speed around 55 mph (88 km/h)
natural_gaits.footfall_pattern: Hind leg, other hind leg, foreleg, other foreleg, followed by suspension
characteristics: Used for short bursts of speed

special_gaits.name: Pace
special_gaits.description: Two-beat lateral gait where legs on same side move together

special_gaits.name: Tölt
special_gaits.description: Four-beat lateral gait with minimal vertical movement

special_gaits.name: Running Walk
special_gaits.description: Smooth, four-beat gait with foot overreaching

phases.name: Landing
phases.description: Return to ground, typically on front legs first

head_tossing.description: Upward, sometimes repeated movement of head

bucking.description: Lowering head and kicking up hind legs

rolling.description: Lying down and rotating body from side to side

learning_capacity.description: Horses' ability to learn and remember

learning_methods.example: Learning to respond to leg pressure
Young horses learning from older herd members

learning_capacity.memory_span: Excellent long-term memory, can remember individuals and training for decades

intelligence_traits.description: Ability to figure out solutions to challenges
Ability to read and respond to emotions in others
Understanding of body position and surroundings

vision.field_of_view: Nearly 360 degrees with blind spots directly in front and behind
vision.night_vision: Better than humans but adjustment time needed

hearing.range: Hear frequencies from 14 Hz to 25 kHz (broader than humans)
hearing.directional_ability: Can rotate ears independently to locate sounds
hearing.sensitivity: More sensitive than human hearing, can detect distant sounds

smell.capacity: Highly developed, better than humans but less than dogs

touch.sensitivity: Extremely sensitive skin, especially muzzle, flanks, and legs
special_features: Can feel a fly landing anywhere on body

taste.preferences: Can distinguish sweet, salty, sour, and bitter
taste.selectivity: Often avoid bitter plants which may be toxic

complex_emotional_states.description: Response to loss, particularly of herd member
Response to perceived preference given to another horse
behavioral_signs: Pushing between handler and other horse

stereotypies.name: Cribbing/Windsucking
stereotypies.description: Grasping surface with teeth, arching neck, and sucking in air

stereotypies.name: Weaving
stereotypies.description: Rhythmic swaying from side to side
